standard-deviation.def: A measure of how far the values in a sample typically sit from their mean: s = √[Σ(x − x̄)² ÷ (n − 1)]. It has the same units as the data, and a larger s means more spread.

standard-error.def: The standard error of the mean, SE = s ÷ √n: an estimate of how much the sample mean would vary if you repeated the whole sample. It shrinks as the sample gets larger.

normal-distribution.def: A symmetric, bell-shaped spread of values around the mean. About 68% of values fall within 1 standard deviation of the mean and about 95% within 2.
